answers.problemDescription: Early-stage SaaS founders waste months building complex features before validating whether customers actually want them. They lack a structured framework to prioritize MVP scope and reduce engineering risk before committing budget.
answers.urgencyDescription: High — founders are actively losing time and money building wrong features. The longer they wait, the more technical debt accumulates and runway shrinks.
answers.alternativesDescription: Most founders rely on informal advice from peers, generic startup templates, or expensive consulting firms that don't understand modern SaaS architecture. None offer a direct founder-to-engineer scoping experience.
answers.productDescription: An AI-powered assessment platform that evaluates a founder's startup readiness, generates a personalized technical roadmap PDF, and recommends the optimal Founder-to-Launch phase. It replaces manual scoping calls with an automated intelligent evaluation.
answers.mvpFeatures: 1. Multi-step assessment wizard with auto-save. 2. AI-powered analysis using Qwen LLM. 3. Automated PDF report generation with framework placement. 4. Founder dashboard with downloadable reports. 5. Google OAuth authentication.
answers.successCriteria: 50 active pilot companies, 5% conversion to paid Discovery Sessions, and securing 3 case studies from early adopters.

reportData.executiveSummary: Parissa is building Vendoroo.AI, an AI-driven scoping and readiness assessment tool designed to help early-stage SaaS founders avoid building the wrong features. The primary opportunity lies in productizing the technical scoping process, turning expensive consulting into an automated, scalable SaaS that guides founders from idea to launch.
founderStrengths: Deep empathy for the exact pain point, having clearly identified the technical debt and wasted runway caused by poor scoping.
Clear vision for productizing a service by transforming manual founder-to-engineer scoping calls into a scalable, AI-driven assessment engine.
Pragmatic MVP definition that focuses on a tight loop of assessment, AI analysis, and PDF generation without getting distracted by unnecessary marketplace features.

biggestOpportunities.title: Productized Technical Scoping
biggestOpportunities.description: By replacing expensive, manual architecture consulting with an AI-driven assessment, you can capture the massive market of bootstrapped founders who cannot afford traditional scoping engagements but desperately need technical direction.

biggestOpportunities.title: The Trojan Horse Lead Gen Engine
biggestOpportunities.description: The assessment naturally funnels highly qualified leads into your paid Discovery Sessions. It acts as an automated top-of-funnel that pre-qualifies founders based on their actual technical readiness and budget.

whatCouldSlowYouDown.risk: Target Audience Mismatch (B2B Enterprise vs. Early-Stage Founders)
whatCouldSlowYouDown.businessImpact: Selling to Enterprise requires long sales cycles, SOC2 compliance, and enterprise pricing, which contradicts the early-stage founder target and bootstrapped reality. This will severely delay initial traction.
whatCouldSlowYouDown.technicalImpact: Building enterprise-grade security, SSO, and audit logging for an MVP aimed at solo founders will bloat the engineering timeline and inflate cloud costs unnecessarily.

whatCouldSlowYouDown.businessImpact: If the Qwen LLM generates technically unsound or generic architectural advice, founders will lose trust immediately, killing the conversion rate to paid sessions and ruining case study potential.
whatCouldSlowYouDown.technicalImpact: Requires building robust prompt engineering, context-window management, and strict output validation layers to ensure the generated PDFs contain actionable SaaS architecture rather than generic fluff.

ifThisWereMyStartup: If this were my startup, I would immediately pivot the target audience from B2B Enterprise to bootstrapped founders and strip out any enterprise-grade requirements from the MVP to get to market in weeks, not months.

Before investing months in development, I would manually run 10 founders through the assessment framework using a simple form and manually generated PDFs to prove they will actually pay for the output before writing a single line of AI integration code.

engineeringStrategy.recommendation: Use Qwen LLM via a structured API with strict JSON schema enforcement for the analysis phase, then use a templating engine like Puppeteer or React-PDF for the final PDF generation.
engineeringStrategy.why: LLMs are great at reasoning but bad at formatting. Separating the AI reasoning from the presentation layer ensures the technical roadmaps look professional and consistent, eliminating AI formatting hallucinations.

engineeringStrategy.recommendation: Next.js frontend with a serverless backend via Vercel and Supabase, integrated with Stripe for subscriptions.
engineeringStrategy.why: As a solo bootstrapped founder, you need maximum leverage. This stack eliminates server management, handles auto-scaling for the assessment wizard, and integrates seamlessly with Google OAuth out-of-the-box.

engineeringStrategy.recommendation: PostgreSQL via Supabase with row-level security and a draft/published state for the assessment wizard.
engineeringStrategy.why: Founders will abandon multi-step wizards. Persisting their progress in a relational database with auto-save ensures high completion rates, and the relational structure easily maps the complex relationships between founders, assessments, and generated reports.

fastestPathToLaunch: Skip the custom UI design for the assessment wizard initially and use a polished, pre-built UI component library like Tailwind UI to get the multi-step wizard live in days.
Hardcode the first three PDF report templates instead of building a dynamic PDF generator; manually tweak the AI output to fit these templates so you can launch and get user feedback immediately.
reportData.recommendedPhaseReasoning: You have a clear problem and a proposed AI solution, but building the full AI assessment engine before proving the underlying scoping framework is a classic trap. In the Validate phase, your only goal is to manually execute the assessment framework for a handful of founders to prove the output is valuable enough to convert them into paid Discovery Sessions, saving you months of premature engineering.
